Combining Atacama Large Millimeter/sub-millimeter Array CO(2-1) mapping and JWST near- and mid-infrared imaging, we characterize the relationship between CO(2-1) and polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) emission at $\approx 100$ pc resolution in 70 nearby star-forming galaxies.
All maps include short- and zero-spacing data and are expected to achieve full flux recovery.
The native resolution is $\approx 1.0\ensuremath{''}$, varying slightly from galaxy to galaxy.
Over the range of distances of the galaxies in the sample, the working resolution for PHANGS–ALMA corresponds to median $98$ pc with a $16{-}84\%$ range of $63{-}129$ pc (cite: leroy2021).

method.value: Compute Spearman rank correlation coefficients, median and MAD scatter of log10(CO/X), bin I_CO(2-1) in logarithmically-spaced bins of MIR intensity I_X, and fit power-law relations using linmix for the full sample, sub-environments, and individual galaxies, as well as fitting galaxy normalizations against M_star and SFR/M_star.

evidence.quote: For each MIR band $X$, we record the Spearman rank correlation coefficient ($r$), as well as the median and scatter in the ratio $I_{\rm CO(2-1)}/I_{\rm X}$. We then calculate a best-fit power law relating $I_{\rm CO(2-1)}$ to $I_{\rm X}$.

We construct logarithmically-spaced bins in $I_\nu^\mathrm{X}$ and then compute the median and scatter, captured by the 16-84% range, of $I_\mathrm{CO(2-1)}$ within each bin. We perform linear regression on these binned measurements using `linmix` a hierarchical Bayesian method described in (cite: kelly2007).

We compute the normalization of the best-fit CO(2-1) versus F770W$_\mathrm{PAH}$ power law for each galaxy, $C_\mathrm{F770W}^\mathrm{PAH}$, by performing a linear fit of $\log_{10}I_\mathrm{CO(2-1)}$ versus $\log_{10}\ensuremath{I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}}$ for each galaxy.

findings_qualitative.value: CO(2-1) and PAH emission (3.3, 7.7, and 11.3 um) exhibit strong, nearly linear correlations at 50-150 pc scales across 70 nearby star-forming galaxies.

evidence.quote: Focusing on regions of galaxies where most of the gas is likely to be molecular, we find strong correlations between CO(2-1) and 3.3 $\mu$m, $7.7\mu$m, and $11.3~\mu$m PAH emission, estimated from JWST’s F335M, F770W, and F1130W filters.

findings_qualitative.value: CO-to-PAH ratios and scaling relations near H II regions are very similar to those in diffuse disk regions, likely because the 70 pc resolution nebular masks include well-shielded molecular gas surrounding the H II regions.

evidence.quote: We find that CO-to-PAH ratios and scaling relationships near H II regions are similar to those in diffuse sight lines.

The similarity of the CO-vs-PAH relationship in diffuse and nebular regions likely results from the fact that the H II region masks that we use (cite: groves2023) are based on data with coarse resolution (median $70$ pc) compared to the actual size of most H II regions (cite: barnes2022).

findings_qualitative.value: Galaxy centers exhibit higher overall intensities and ~0.16-0.2 dex (~60%) higher CO-to-PAH ratios compared to galaxy disks, likely driven by lower X_CO in galaxy centers.

evidence.quote: On average the CO-to-PAH ratio is $\approx 0.16$ dex ($\approx 60\%$) higher in galaxy centers compared to disks, and the median $I_{\rm CO(2-1)}$ in centers appear higher than that found for disks at fixed $I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}$.
may indicate that $X_{\rm CO}$ represents the dominant effect, offsetting these other PAH-enhancing effects.

findings_qualitative.value: Galaxy-to-galaxy normalizations of CO at fixed PAH intensity correlate positively with stellar mass and anti-correlate with specific star formation rate.

evidence.quote: Consistent with previous work we find a mild positive correlation between the CO/PAH ratio at fixed $I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}$ and $M_\star$ and an anti-correlation between the CO/PAH normalization and $\mathrm{SFR}/M_\star$.

claims.hypothesis: PAH emission in JWST NIR and MIR bands correlates with and scales nearly linearly with CO(2-1) emission at molecular cloud scales (50-150 pc) across the nearby star-forming galaxy population.
claims.experiment: Compare resolution-matched ALMA CO(2-1) and JWST F335M_PAH, F770W_PAH, and F1130W intensities across 70 PHANGS galaxies at ~100 pc resolution and fit power-law scaling relations with linmix.
claims.result: Rank correlations r = 0.58 to 0.64 across all pixels, with power-law slopes m = 0.8 to 1.3 (e.g., m = 0.90 +- 0.07 for F770W_PAH, m = 1.01 +- 0.10 for F335M_PAH, m = 1.02 +- 0.09 for F1130W).
claims.finding: Strong, approximately linear scaling relationships exist between CO(2-1) and 3.3, 7.7, and 11.3 um PAH emission at 50-150 pc scales.

evidence.quote: We derive power law relations between CO(2-1) and PAH emission, which have indices in the range $0.8{-}1.3$, implying relatively weak variations in the observed CO-to-PAH ratios across the regions that we study.
CO(2-1) exhibits strong correlations with the PAH emission captured by JWST’s F770W, F335M, and F1130W filters.

claims.hypothesis: CO-to-PAH ratios and scaling relations differ significantly between nebular (H II) regions and diffuse disk regions due to PAH destruction inside H II regions.
claims.experiment: Apply VLT/MUSE nebular masks to 19 Cycle 1 galaxies to separate disk sight lines into nebular and diffuse regions and compare their CO-to-PAH ratios and power-law fits.
claims.result: Median CO/F770W_PAH in H II regions is -0.02 +- 0.34 dex vs 0.08 +- 0.38 dex in diffuse regions (~0.10 dex difference), with similar power-law scaling relations.
claims.finding: At ~100 pc resolution, CO-to-PAH ratios and scaling relations near H II regions are very similar to diffuse regions, except nebular sight lines have higher overall intensities, likely because the 70 pc masks blend H II regions with surrounding shielded gas.

evidence.quote: We find that CO-to-PAH ratios and scaling relationships near H II regions are similar to those in diffuse sight lines. The main difference between the two types of regions is that sight lines near H II regions show higher intensities in all tracers.

Perhaps surprisingly, we find median CO/F770W$_\mathrm{PAH}$ ratios in H II and diffuse regions to be quite similar, with H II regions exhibiting a ratio only $\approx 0.10$ dex ($1.25\times$) lower than diffuse regions (i.e., PAHs are slightly brighter relatively to CO near H II regions).

claims.hypothesis: Galaxy centers exhibit different CO-to-PAH ratios compared to galaxy disks due to extreme ISM conditions and lower X_CO.
claims.experiment: Use morphological center masks across 70 galaxies to compare CO-to-PAH ratios and power-law fits in galaxy centers versus disks.
claims.result: Median log10(CO/F770W_PAH) is 0.18 +- 0.33 in centers vs 0.02 +- 0.35 outside centers, an enhancement of ~0.16 dex (~60%).
claims.finding: Galaxy centers show higher overall intensities and systematically enhanced CO-to-PAH ratios compared to galaxy disks, consistent with suppressed X_CO in centers dominating over stronger radiation fields.

evidence.quote: On average the CO-to-PAH ratio is $\approx 0.16$ dex ($\approx 60\%$) higher in galaxy centers compared to disks, and the median $I_{\rm CO(2-1)}$ in centers appear higher than that found for disks at fixed $I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}$.

We also contrast galaxy centers with emission from the surrounding disks, finding that galaxy centers exhibit on average an $\approx 0.2$ dex ($\approx 60\%$) higher ratio of CO(2-1)-to-F770W emission compared to galaxy disks (cite: pathak2024).

claims.hypothesis: Galaxy-to-galaxy variations in the CO(2-1)-to-PAH normalization correlate with global galaxy properties that trace radiation field strength and ISM properties.
claims.experiment: Fit the CO-PAH normalization C_band at I_PAH = 1 MJy sr^-1 for each of the 70 galaxies and perform linear regressions against log10(M_star) and log10(SFR/M_star).
claims.result: Galaxy normalizations scatter by +-0.17 dex (0.19 dex in abstract) and correlate with log10(M_star) (slope 0.15 +- 0.04, r = 0.38) and anti-correlate with log10(SFR/M_star) (slope -0.21 +- 0.04, r = -0.50).
claims.finding: Galaxy-to-galaxy offsets in CO/PAH normalization are not random; they anti-correlate with specific star formation rate and correlate with stellar mass, allowing an empirical renormalization prescription.

evidence.quote: Consistent with previous work we find a mild positive correlation between the CO/PAH ratio at fixed $I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}$ and $M_\star$ and an anti-correlation between the CO/PAH normalization and $\mathrm{SFR}/M_\star$.

Individual galaxies show similar relations between CO(2-1) and PAH intensity, but with $\approx \pm 0.2$ dex scatter in the normalization. The ratio of CO at fixed PAH intensity for a galaxy correlates with its stellar mass, $M_\star$, and anti-correlates with its specific star formation rate SFR/$M_\star$, in good agreement with results for integrated galaxies using WISE.

why_this_data.value: Combining PHANGS-JWST Cycle 1 and 2 treasuries with PHANGS-ALMA CO(2-1) expands the sample of ~100 pc resolution CO-PAH comparisons by over an order of magnitude to 70 galaxies, while flat CO maps ensure >90% flux completeness without S/N clipping bias.

evidence.quote: Leveraging a new Cycle 2 JWST treasury program targeting nearby galaxies, we expand the sample size by more than an order of magnitude compared to previous $\approx 100$ pc resolution CO-PAH comparisons.

We use a noisy but uniform and high-completeness version of the CO (2-1) maps to ensure that $>90\,\%$ of the CO flux enters our analysis and that our mean trends will be unbiased by signal-to-noise based clipping of the CO data (cite: leroy2023).

why_this_method.value: Because ALMA CO maps are much less sensitive than JWST MIR maps at matched resolution, MIR intensity is used as the independent x-axis and CO is averaged in logarithmic bins before Bayesian linear regression with linmix, avoiding S/N clipping bias.

evidence.quote: Because the PHANGS–ALMA CO maps are much less sensitive than the JWST F770W and F1130W maps at matched angular resolution (cite: leroy2023), we treat the mid-IR imaging as the independent ($x$) axis for this calculation.

We construct logarithmically-spaced bins in $I_\nu^\mathrm{X}$ and then compute the median and scatter, captured by the 16-84% range, of $I_\mathrm{CO(2-1)}$ within each bin. We perform linear regression on these binned measurements using `linmix` a hierarchical Bayesian method described in (cite: kelly2007).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Adopting a CO-to-H2 conversion factor was rejected for the main analysis to avoid introducing systematic uncertainties.

evidence.quote: To avoid introducing systematic uncertainties, we analyze CO(2-1) intensities and do not adopt a CO-to-H$_2$ conversion factor.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Subtracting hot dust continuum from F770W was rejected because it has a small effect.

evidence.quote: The F770W filter also captures emission from hot, very small dust grains, but this has a small effect (cite: baron2024a) and we do not subtract any underlying dust continuum.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Analyzing Cycle 2 F335M data was deferred because the F300M-based stellar continuum subtraction for Cycle 2 is not yet science-ready.

evidence.quote: Both the JWST Cycle 1 and Cycle 2 data include the F335M filter but the continuum subtraction needed to isolate the PAH emission has only reached a science-ready state for the Cycle 1 data (§3.1).

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: NGC 3344, NGC 5530, and NGC 1068 were excluded from the Cycle 2 sample due to lack of CO(2-1) data, unexecuted observations, and uncertain JWST background levels, respectively.

evidence.quote: From the 54 available Cycle 2 galaxies, we remove NGC 3344 due to the lack of CO (2-1) observations, NGC 5530 because the observations are still to be executed, and NGC 1068 because the background level in the JWST images remain too uncertain for the current analysis.

limitations_admitted.value: Results only apply to bright, molecular gas-dominated regions (I_F770W^PAH >= 0.5 MJy sr^-1, Sigma_mol >= 4 M_sun pc^-2) and exclude 49% of the map area outside galaxy centers and nebulae where H I dominates.

evidence.quote: However, we do exclude a majority ($49\%$) of the area in the maps outside galaxy centers and nebulae. Analysis of this faint, extended diffuse emission requires the inclusion of H I and will be the topic of future work.
Our results formally apply to regions where molecular gas is likely to constitute a significant fraction of the ISM, with $\Sigma_{\rm mol} \gtrsim 4$ M$_\odot$ pc$^{-2}$.

limitations_admitted.value: Sightline-to-sightline scatter in CO at low PAH intensity is large (~0.5 dex) and dominated by statistical noise (~1 K km s^-1) in the flat PHANGS-ALMA CO maps.

evidence.quote: At lower $I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}$, which corresponds to most of the area, the scatter in CO at fixed $I^\mathrm{PAH}_{\rm F770W}$ appears somewhat higher, $\pm 0.5$ dex. Much of this reflects the statistical noise in the PHANGS–ALMA CO maps, which often approaches $\approx \pm 1$ K km s$^{-1}$ in the “flat” CO maps that we use.

limitations_admitted.value: Nebular region masks have coarse physical resolution (median 70 pc) compared to true H II region sizes, blending emission from inside H II regions with surrounding shielded molecular gas.

evidence.quote: The similarity of the CO-vs-PAH relationship in diffuse and nebular regions likely results from the fact that the H II region masks that we use (cite: groves2023) are based on data with coarse resolution (median $70$ pc) compared to the actual size of most H II regions (cite: barnes2022).

limitations_admitted.value: Hot dust continuum is not subtracted from F770W, which could affect regions where PAHs are destroyed or galaxy centers where hot dust is stronger.

evidence.quote: Subtracting hot dust continuum emission from F770W, which we do not do, may also be important, since the filter still captures such emission in regions where PAHs have been destroyed to the point where their emission is not detectable.

Finally, we note that we do not subtract any hot dust continuum from F770W. Hot dust continuum is likely stronger in galaxy centers, implying that our reported CO-to-PAH ratio measurements are lower than the true ratios.

limitations_admitted.value: Predicting molecular gas surface density N(H2) from predicted CO(2-1) requires an environment-dependent CO-to-H2 conversion factor, which is not included in the empirical CO-PAH relations.

evidence.quote: The CO(2-1)-to-H$_2$ conversion factor is known to vary as a function of environment across galaxies and this will need to be included to predict the gas column density, $N({\rm H}_2)$ (cite: bolatto2013; schinnerer2024).

referee_caveats_inferred: Cycle 2 JWST reductions and F335M continuum subtraction rely on several in-preparation papers (Koziol et al., Pathak et al., Weinbeck et al.), making exact replication of the Cycle 2 background anchoring and F335M continuum subtraction dependent on unpublished details.
Spatial pixels of size FWHM/3 oversample the beam (9 pixels per independent beam area), which affects formal statistical uncertainties if pixels are treated as independent prior to binning.

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Tens of GB for processed 2D CO(2-1) moment maps and JWST mosaics across 70 galaxies (several TB if starting from raw ALMA visibilities and uncalibrated JWST exposures)
reproducibility.score_reason: The statistical analysis, pixel gridding, thresholds, and fitting methods (linmix, webbpsf, pjpipe) are clearly described and high-level PHANGS-ALMA and PHANGS-JWST products are publicly archived, but several preprocessing details (flat CO map velocity windows, F335M continuum subtraction coefficients from in-prep work, star masks, and exact bin widths) are not explicitly stated in the paper.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: The main findings are clean numerical power-law scaling relations and correlation coefficients across 70 galaxies using public PHANGS-ALMA and PHANGS-JWST treasury datasets, making it well-suited for reproducing the CO-PAH scaling relations from processed maps.
